title: Scotland Had Not Won a World Cup Match in 36 Years. John McGinn Changed That in Foxborough.
excerpt: A deflected strike in the 28th minute put the Scots atop Group C ahead of Brazil and Morocco, in front of 64,146 fans at the Boston Stadium
body:
Scotland had not won a World Cup match since beating Sweden 2-1 in Genoa at Italia '90. On Saturday night at the Boston Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, John McGinn ended that 36-year drought with a single deflected strike in the 28th minute.

Haiti 0, Scotland 1. Group C belongs to the Scots — for now.

## The Goal That Ended the Wait

It was not the prettiest strike in World Cup history. McGinn's shot from the edge of the box took two deflections on its way past goalkeeper Johny Placide and into the net. But as every Scotland fan among the 64,146 in attendance would tell you, nobody cared about aesthetics.

It was Scotland's first World Cup goal since Craig Burley lobbed the goalkeeper against Norway in the summer of 1998, 28 years ago. The Tartan Army erupted, and the opening bars of *Yes Sir, I Can Boogie* echoed through the stadium speakers.

"All that mattered was that there was one magical moment from John McGinn," wrote the Scottish Sun. "The best a nation could get."

## Haiti's Near Miss

Steve Clarke's side rode their luck in the second half. Scott McTominay, the Manchester United midfielder, looked sluggish after a bout of illness and did not have his sharpest night. Haiti, playing their first World Cup match in 52 years, grew in confidence as the game wore on.

The closest they came to an equaliser arrived in the 85th minute. Frantzdy Pierrot — who moved from Haiti to nearby Melrose, Massachusetts, at age 11 and was named Gatorade Player of the Year at Malden Catholic High School — rose to meet a cross and nodded a header that drifted agonisingly wide of the left post.

Six minutes of stoppage time followed. Scotland held on, occasionally by their fingernails, but they held on.

## Group C Standings After Day 3

Scotland now sit atop Group C with three points. Brazil and Morocco, who drew 1-1 at MetLife Stadium earlier on Saturday, have one point each. Haiti remain on zero.

The Scots face Morocco back at the Boston Stadium on Friday, June 19. Haiti travel to the Philadelphia Stadium the same day to face Brazil — a daunting assignment for a team that showed spirit but lacked the finishing touch.

## The NRI Angle

For the thousands of Indian-Americans in the Boston metro area, the World Cup has arrived on their doorstep. The Boston Stadium in Foxborough — a 30-mile drive from downtown — is hosting six group-stage matches this tournament. With tickets still available for several fixtures, NRIs in New England have a rare opportunity to experience football's biggest stage without leaving the Northeast.

Scotland's next match against Morocco, in particular, could attract a large diaspora turnout. Morocco's run to the 2022 World Cup semifinals captivated fans across the globe, and the Atlas Lions remain one of the tournament's most compelling storylines. If you are in the area, The Videshi's NRI Guide for the Boston Stadium venue has everything you need to plan your trip.
